data.name: Khokhar
data.gender_notes: Khokhar is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Krishna' which means 'black' and 'kharah' which means 'soil'. This name symbolizes the fertile and rich earth which nurtures and provides life. The name Khokhar carries the meaning “Black Soil” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Khokhar usually hope their child will grow to embody black soil and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine earth element and the power of creation.
data.etymology: Khokhar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Black Soil.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khokhar total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu mythology, 'Krishna' is an avatar of the god Vishnu, and the name has been celebrated in various Hindu scriptures and folklore. The name 'Khokhar' can be seen as a symbol of the fertile and rich earth, which is considered a giver of life. It represents the earth's ability to nurture and provide sustenance to all living beings. In rural Hindu communities, the name 'Khokhar' may also be given to a child born on land that is considered fertile and productive.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Khokhar' also holds great spiritual significance for Hindus. The word 'Krishna' itself is believed to be a manifestation of divine love and protection. The 'kharah' or soil symbolizes the ground on which all living beings exist and eventually return to. This name reminds us of the interconnectedness and interdependence of all beings, and the role of the earth in the cycle of birth, life, and death. The name 'Khokhar' can serve as a reminder of the importance of honoring and respecting the earth as a sacred entity and recognizing its invaluable role in our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Khokhar in Hinduism is believed to originate from the Sanskrit word "Khoka," which means a thief or one who steals. However, it is also considered a playful name for those who possess a mischievous or playful spirit, as in Hindu mythology, the god Krishna, a prankster and trickster, is often referred to as Khokha.

historical_references.reference: The Khokhars were a Rajput clan that ruled over the region of Jhelum and Sialkot in the Punjab during the medieval period.
